description: Gen Worlds is a browser game in which one to four players plan a NASA-style mission and then fly it. Players choose the spacecraft's systems, the rocket, the route and the dates while nine live budgets (mass, propellant, launch, power, night, data, cost, schedule, risk) explain in plain language what each choice costs. summary:
Gen Worlds is a browser game in which one to four players plan a NASA-style mission and then fly it.

Players choose the spacecraft's systems, the rocket, the route and the dates while nine live budgets (mass, propellant, launch, power, night, data, cost, schedule, risk) explain in plain language what each choice costs.

A deterministic simulation built on real orbital mechanics and NASA data then plays the mission out, and the debrief traces every outcome back to the decision that caused it.

Additionally a procedually generated sandbox galaxy to fly and play with.
details:
GEN WORLDS - PROJECT DETAILS

============================

WHAT IT DOES

------------

A mission runs in six steps, the same ones a real project goes through.

1. Briefing

Science objectives with their weights, the budget cap, and the resources that usually decide the mission.

2. Hangar

A part for every system: frame, power, battery, propulsion, attitude control, computer, radio, thermal control, mobility, landing system and up to six instruments. Each part card shows what choosing it would do to the budgets before you commit, and the spacecraft is rebuilt in 3D as you choose.

3. Trajectory

The rocket (payload against launch energy or orbit altitude), the route and the dates. For the Moon, a calendar of sunlight and Earth visibility at each landing site computed from the lunar ephemeris. For Mars, a porkchop plot computed with a Lambert solver, with the arrivals too fast for the heat shield greyed out. For Earth orbit, the altitude trade between image detail, ground contact, drag lifetime and the five-year debris rule.

4. Go/No-Go poll

Each of four roles (Flight Director, Spacecraft Engineer, Science Lead, Comms and Operations) answers for its part of the mission. A Monte Carlo forecast flies the design 200 times and shows how often it works and what usually goes wrong.

5. Flight

The mission plays out day by day on a 3D stage that shows your own vehicle lifting off, coasting, landing and working, beside a dashboard of sunlight, Earth in view, battery and data, hour by hour. On the Moon and on Mars the player can fly the last kilometres of the landing by hand in 3D over the real terrain, with the propellant the design left.

6. Debrief

Score, objectives, and a list of findings: each names the design decision behind an outcome and links to the screen where it can be changed. Runs are compared side by side.

Additionally, a procedually generated galaxy sandbox to play with.

HOW IT ADDRESSES THE CHALLENGE

------------------------------

Define objectives and requirements

- Briefing with weighted objectives; instruments must cover them.

Design spacecraft and payload

- Hangar with 60+ parts, live budgets, 3D vehicle.

Select launch vehicle and orbit

- Trajectory screen: capacity chart, porkchop plot, orbit trade.

Manage budget, mass, power, communications, data, duration

- Nine budget lines, each with a plain-language "why"; mission dashboard in flight.

Simulate and evaluate

- Deterministic hour-by-hour simulation, 200-run forecast, causal debrief.

1 to 4 players with distinct roles and shared decisions

- Four roles that each own part of the design, requests between roles, Go/No-Go poll, events routed to roles in flight, coordination score; on one screen or one device each.

Different skill levels

- Three difficulty levels, a tutorial mission, step-by-step explainers, glossary; plays without WebGPU.

Clear feedback, rerun

- Findings traced to decisions, one click back to the design, run comparison.

Multiple scenarios and random events

- Three NASA-based missions, plus a mission on any solid world of a generated galaxy, chosen from a 3D galaxy map or by flying there; seeded events (budget cuts, solar storms, dust storms, wheel faults, station outages) that the design can mitigate.

Compare and share

- Links that reproduce a flight exactly, daily mission, leaderboard that re-flies every entry.

Education

- Every number explained; "How NASA approached it" card per mission.

WHY IT MATTERS

--------------

Spaceflight is the art of living inside budgets, and that is hard to feel from a lecture. Here the kilogram you add to the rover becomes two kilograms of propellant and a bigger rocket in front of you; the battery you skimped on freezes the rover in a polar night whose length came from the real Moon. Because the simulation is deterministic, two players can fly the same seed and argue about the design instead of the dice.

HOW WE BUILT IT

---------------

- TypeScript, Vite, Preact for the 2D screens, three.js (WebGPU) for the 3D.

- One mission model in pure functions (design -> budgets; design + seed + inputs -> result), shared by the budgets, the forecast, the flight, the debrief and the leaderboard check, covered by 118 unit tests. It runs in a web worker for the forecast.

- All numbers live in JSON data files with their sources; no balance values in code.

- Deployed as a static site on GitHub Pages; online rooms and the leaderboard use Firebase (Firestore, anonymous sign-in) and the game plays fully without them.
